Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Petroleum Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Petroleum Corp.'s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer; Tom Bradley, VP of Exploration; Rachel Kim, VP of Marketing; David Patel, Chief Sustainability Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Apex Petroleum Corp. delivered solid results in Q3 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved robust production growth of 18% year-over-year to 285,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, with oil making up 72% of the mix, alongside a standout EBITDA increase of 28% to $1.85 billion. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on capital allocation, prioritizing sustainable dividends, opportunistic share buybacks, and high-return reinvestments that are compounding value for shareholders. We are focused on maintaining a strong balance sheet with net debt at $12.7 billion and leverage at 1.8 times EBITDAX. Further, we are working on proved reserves additions totaling 682 million BOE for the full year, achieving a 133% reserve replacement ratio including 108% organically. We continue to adjust to efficient capital expenditures, coming in under budget through drilling, completion, and facilities optimizations. We are advancing future development plans across our Tier 1 assets like the Permian, with multi-year inventory visibility. We are evaluating midstream infrastructure expansions that drove record transportation volumes. Finally, we are taking steps to integrate technology and sustainability initiatives, from AI-driven analytics to CCUS pilots, positioning us for long-term resilience.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Harlan to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Mike Harlan: Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $5.2 billion, up 25% year-over-year, reflecting higher realized prices and volumes. Operating income was $1.1 billion, and net income was $850 million. We generated $1.8 billion in free cash flow—bringing year-to-date to $5.2 billion after upstream capex and debt reduction—and returned $500 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $14.8 billion in total debt, $2.1 billion in cash, and net debt at $12.7 billion.

Let me dive deeper into our EBITDA performance, which came in at $1.85 billion for the quarter, a robust 28% increase from $1.44 billion in Q3 2023. On a trailing twelve months basis, adjusted EBITDA now stands at $7.2 billion, up 22% year-over-year, highlighting the strength of our integrated upstream portfolio and payoffs from multi-year efficiency programs. Key drivers start with the top line: realized oil prices averaged $78.50 per barrel, up 15% from $68.20 last year, thanks to Brent in the mid-$80s from OPEC+ cuts and global demand recovery. Natural gas realizations were steady at $3.45 per Mcf, supported by Henry Hub at $3.10 and hedging 65% of Q4 volumes at a $3.80 floor. NGLs added value at $28.50 per barrel, up 12% on Mont Belvieu pricing.

Production volumes grew 18% to 285,000 BOE per day, with Permian net output at 180,000 BOE/d, up 25%, from Delaware Basin pads with 450 new horizontals averaging 12,000-foot laterals. Our Super Frac design using dissolvable diverters and ceramic proppants delivered initial rates of 1,800 BOE/d per well, 20% above type curve, complemented by AI predictive analytics from our Halliburton partnership that cut unplanned downtime by 35%. Eagle Ford added 12% growth to 45,000 BOE/d via refracs on low-decline wells. Gulf of Mexico rose 8% to 35,000 BOE/d with Lucius Phase 2 tie-back using subsea boosting. North Sea dipped 5% on declines but was offset by a $250 million acquisition of high-pressure prospects.

Costs contributed $450 million in uplift, with lifting costs down 14% to $9.20 per BOE from supply chain deals cutting proppant 22% and Nabors automated rigs reducing drilling times to 12 days per well. DD&A stayed flat at $14.50 per BOE due to reservoir management and 4D seismic upgrades to 15% of proved developed producing reserves. This validates our framework: 55% of cash flow to Permian development, 20% to a $1.5 billion buyback now 40% complete. Our 32% margin expansion beats peers, per Wood Mackenzie.

Turning to capital allocation priorities, with WTI at $82 per barrel and Henry Hub at $2.90 per MMBtu from LNG demand, our framework maximizes total shareholder return. First, sustainable dividends: we're raising our quarterly payout 12% to $0.52 per share, or $2.08 annualized, yielding 3.8%—our fifth straight hike, with $1.1 billion in 2024 scaling to $1.4 billion in 2025 at 1.8x coverage even at $70 WTI. Second, share buybacks: new $3 billion authorization atop $500 million remaining; YTD $1.2 billion repurchased at $52 average, retiring 2.1% of shares for 4% EPS accretion, targeting 5-7% reduction annually when below $65 NAV. Third, reinvestment at over 25% IRR: $4.2 billion 2024 capex, 85% upstream—$2.7 billion Permian for 180 net wells with 14,000-foot laterals and enhanced completions; $630 million Bakken/Eagle Ford; $420 million international like Vaca Muerta JV and Guyana; $420 million tech/sustainability including CCUS and AI. Balance to debt reduction, net debt at 0.9x EBITDAX.

On debt levels, total gross debt is $14.8 billion, down from $16.2 billion year-end 2023 after $1.2 billion term loan repayments. Breakdown: $8.5 billion notes at 4.4% average coupon, 7.2-year maturity; $250 million RCF draw on $4 billion capacity; minimal short-term. Net debt $12.7 billion after $2.1 billion cash from $1.8 billion Q3 cash flow. Leverage at 1.8x TTM EBITDAX, down from 2.6x, below 2.0x target—better than peers. Coverage 8.5x, with $1.1 billion Bakken divestiture, refinancing, RBL up 10% to $10.2 billion on 2.8 Bboe reserves, and 55% 2025 oil hedged.

For capex guidance, 2025 spend is $6.0 to $6.5 billion, up 10%, funded at $70 WTI. 65% or $3.9-$4.2 billion upstream development: 250-275 Permian wells at 60% IRR, sub-$35 breakeven. 15% exploration: Permian wildcats, Gulf Salazar Deep. 20% maintenance/midstream/low-carbon: CCUS, electrification, digital twins. Permian 70%, Eagle Ford/Gulf/international balanced. Targets >20% IRR, 50%+ FCF payout.

I will now turn the call over to Lisa Chen for an operational update.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Mike. On the operational front, we continue to execute effectively. Our production averaged 285,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought Delaware Basin pads online, contributing to growth with initial rates 20% above curve. We're advancing cost reductions, with lifting costs at $9.20 per BOE and drilling efficiencies via automated rigs.

Now I will turn it over to Tom Bradley for an update on our exploration activities.

Tom Bradley: Thank you, Lisa. We're excited about our program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Basin and are planning to drill 50 exploration wells next year. These have potential to add significant reserves. For the full year 2023, we added 682 million BOE to proved developed producing and non-producing reserves net of revisions, against 512 million BOE produced at 1.4 million BOE per day average—yielding 133% total reserve replacement ratio above our 120% target, and 108% organic excluding minor acquisitions. Extensions/discoveries drove 412 million BOE, revisions 189 million from performance and $71.37 WTI SEC prices, improved recovery 81 million via EOR. Permian added 298 million BOE at 185% organic RRR from Wolfcamp/Bone Spring extensions; Eagle Ford 142 million at 125%; Gulf 156 million including Loki discovery; international 86 million from Stabroek and North Sea EOR. Tech like ML seismic, RSS, CO2 pilots cut risks. Three-year organic RRR 112%, 12+ year inventory.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Rachel Kim to discuss our marketing strategy.

Rachel Kim: Thank you, Tom. We are focused on optimizing to maximize production value. Strong demand for our Super Frac outputs in the Permian Basin, expanding customer base. Impact is significant, with midstream at 45% of EBITDA. Q3 transportation volumes hit record 1.85 million barrels per day equivalents, up 18% YoY: 1.2 million crude up 22% via Waco Express at 95% utilization, $1.05 tariffs, Waha tight -$0.15; 3.2 Bcf/d gas up 12%, 85% take-or-pay; 450,000 bbls/d NGLs up 15%. Revenues $1.45 billion, margins 52%. Capex $750 million YTD: Permian Link 550,000 bbls/d online, Appalachia Connector 1.2 Bcf/d nearing completion, Mont Belvieu frac train.

I will now turn it over to David Patel to discuss our sustainability efforts.

David Patel: Thank you, Rachel. We're committed to reducing our footprint. Significant progress on greenhouse gas emissions via electrification and methane detection under OGMP 2.0, flaring under 1%. Investing in renewables, CCUS pilots capturing 1.5 million mtpa CO2 for EOR and 45Q credits, water recycling at 85%, protecting biodiversity through drone monitoring.

I will now turn the call over to Elena Vasquez to discuss our technology initiatives.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, David. We're leveraging tech for efficiency, cost reduction, safety. Investments in automation, data analytics, AI for predictive maintenance optimizing chokes, frac designs via digital twins on Delfi platform cutting cycle times 12%, dry hole risk 30%. Exploring CCUS, rig electrification displacing 30% diesel.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on proved reserves additions, reserve replacement ratio, and organic growth?

Tom Bradley: Good morning, Sarah. Maintaining a strong reserve replacement ratio is key for sustainability at current WTI around $75. Full year 2023 added 682 million BOE net to PDP and PDNP against 512 million produced, for 133% total RRR up from 115%, and 108% organic—third straight year over 100% without big M&A. Breakdown: 412 million extensions/discoveries, 189 million positive revisions from performance and SEC prices, 81 million improved recovery, minimal purchases, negligible negative revisions. Organic 670 million added. Permian 298 million BOE, 185% organic from 18 new locations; Eagle Ford 142 million, 125% from Austin Chalk; Gulf 156 million with Loki; international 86 million Stabroek/North Sea. Tech investments $450 million in ML seismic, RSS, CO2 EOR. Three-year 112% organic, 12-year inventory, $1.2 billion 2024 capex for 130% RRR.

Operator: Our next question comes from John Ramirez with Exxon Capital. Please go ahead.

John Ramirez: Good morning. Could you walk us through the CapEx breakdown for Drilling, Completion, and Facilities—budget vs. actual year-to-date, variances, and ties to Permian pads?

Mike Harlan: Absolutely, John. Great chance to highlight execution. Guided $2.4 billion 2024, 55% drilling, 35% completion, 10% facilities. YTD $1.95 billion, 81% pace, full-year $2.3-2.35 billion, 4-7% under. Drilling: budget $1.32 billion, YTD $1.05 billion, 5% under from Permian efficiencies—52 wells vs. 48 planned, 18.5 days per mile with RSS, PDC bits; Permian $735 million vs. $780 million. Completion: $840 million budget, $710 million YTD, slight over from sand but offsetting with slickwater 2,500 lbs/ft, electric fleets; Permian $535 million. Facilities: $240 million budget, $190 million, 13% under modularization, water recycling. Underspend funds FCF, ROIC >50%.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Energy Capital Partners. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: What are your future development plans and resource potential, including inventory life?

Alex Rivera: Great question, Sarah. I'll start and turn to Lisa. Mike Harlan: Thanks, Alex. Year-end 2023: 1.2 billion BOE 1P, 3.8 billion 2P up 15%, 6.1 billion 3P; 180% RRR. 18,000 locations, 1.1 million BOE EUR average, 15-year inventory. Permian 65% 2P, 4,500 Delaware locations, 2-mile laterals 2,400 BOEPD IP; Eagle Ford 1.2 billion BOE; Guyana 150 million net; GOM 500 million. 2024-2026 $4.2 billion capex, production to 750 mbopd 10% CAGR. Innovations: Frac of the Future 12% recovery uplift, AI modeling $650/foot D&C, CCUS 2 MMTPA. Hedged 60% oil, opportunistic M&A.

Operator: Our next question comes from Brian Walsh with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Brian Walsh: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Tom Bradley: The exploration success, like Loki and Stabroek extensions, reinforces our focus on Tier 1 assets, extending inventory and supporting 5-7% growth with low-risk additions at >25% IRR.

Operator: Our next question comes from Laura Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Laura Chen: What is the outlook for midstream transportation and new infrastructure?

Rachel Kim: Volumes to grow 10-12% 2025 on Permian DUCs, Haynesville efficiencies. $15 billion contracted backlog, deleveraging to 3.6x, ESG via leak detection.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mark Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mark Patel: Could you elaborate on your sustainability targets?

David Patel: Targets include Scope 1 down 18% YoY, 2 MMTPA CO2 by 2026, 85% water recycle, <1% flaring via Seekir monitoring and electrification.

Operator: Our next question comes from Dana Lee with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Dana Lee: What are the key technology initiatives you are focused on?

Elena Vasquez: AI seismic inversion, digital twins reducing risks 30%, dissolvable diverters lifting EURs 15%, CCUS for 45Q and recovery, electric rigs 30% diesel cut.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
